title: Emailer Ripe user manual
subtitle: Version 1.3.6 | Accounts, setup and everyday newsletters

blocks.text: Prepare, test, approve, then send. Saving a draft sends nothing. A campaign is one newsletter, a template is reusable content, and a list is a group of contacts.

Ubuntu 26.04 uses its maintained distribution PHP 8.5 packages; no external PHP source is added. A compatible existing MariaDB 10.11 or 11.8 service is reused without a major upgrade. Setup adds a dedicated Emailer PHP-FPM pool and keeps existing website pools, PHP alternatives and Virtualmin-managed websites in place. Missing PHP extension packages add their standard extension configuration; existing PHP settings are retained and shared PHP services are not restarted.

Ubuntu 26.04.1 / Virtualmin coexistence uses a spare Emailer hostname and preserves the existing Virtualmin domains and PHP pools. Setup creates its own Apache site; it does not register a Virtualmin domain. Keep that site under Emailer installer management. Light 1.2.4 and 1.2.6 on Ubuntu 26.04 upgrade directly to Ripe 1.3.6; the original Light signing identity, administrator credentials and installation identity are retained. Delivery remains held until the guided readiness acceptance.

Ubuntu 26.04.1 HTTPS acceptance used a local ACME server with real HTTP challenge validation and strict certificate/name verification. Public certificate issuance remains unverified because no dedicated non-production hostname and DNS authority were available. Customer setup uses the normal public ACME service; DNS must point to the server and Apache must be reachable on ports 80 and 443.

Ripe’s Ubuntu Apache installer supports wildcard and literal address-specific virtual hosts on explicit ports 80 and 443. Light retains a wildcard-only Apache profile. An existing Nginx service on a separate port, such as 8081, remains unchanged.

The 1.3.6 setup file supports Ubuntu 22.04/24.04/26.04 with Apache and Debian 13 with Nginx. It creates a dedicated PHP runtime, application services, backups and a command launcher. Ubuntu 22.04 gets an isolated supported database beside existing sites. Administrator email is the default login name on fresh setup; existing accounts keep their identifier and password. You can sign in, prepare templates and campaigns, and configure SMTP later. See the beginner installation guide for the tested hosting profile and one-file setup action.
Your installed account

The fresh installer creates an Owner using your administrator email. Existing accounts keep their identifiers and password hashes. For Light transitions, follow the upgrade guide. Fresh organisation defaults are Emailer, English and UTC. The installer installs background services and an initial encrypted backup. You can prepare content and drafts while sending is blocked.

blocks.caption: Actual Ripe dashboard with email delivery deferred.

blocks.text: Choose your dashboard appearance

Open Appearance in the administration header. Studio gives a crisp, structured workspace; Warm adds welcoming colours and gentle motion; Website uses saved organisation branding. Classic keeps the original look. Fresh Ripe installations start with Studio. An update or Light upgrade keeps the existing Classic appearance until you choose another skin.

items: Choose a thumbnail to preview its skin immediately. Anything you have typed on the page stays in place.
Choose Save appearance to keep your choice across sign-ins. Your selection affects only your account.
Choose Revert preview, Cancel or Escape to return to your saved appearance.
For less animation choose Reduce motion. Otherwise Emailer follows your device’s motion preference.

blocks.caption: The actual Appearance dialog: preview a skin, reduce motion, save or revert.
Studio keeps administration tables and operational status readable.
Warm applies the same presentation to settings and forms; permissions and sending checks stay in place.

blocks.text: Match your organisation website

In Appearance choose Website. An Administrator or Owner can confirm or edit the suggested address, or enter the organisation’s public HTTPS website, and choose Refresh from website and save for everyone. Confirm the organisation website rather than assuming that the Emailer dashboard address is the right source. No website is contacted until you press this button.

Emailer saves a small set of colours, a system or serif heading font and, when available, a small safe site icon. It does not copy whole pages or load the website into your dashboard. If no suitable icon is found, the text mark remains. The source address and last refresh time are displayed. Extraction suggests a coherent starting point; it cannot exactly copy every website.

items: Review the preview. Adjust Primary, Accent, Panels, Page background, Text and Headings if needed.
Choose Save corrected branding for everyone to share your corrections with accounts using Website. These shared branding buttons save immediately; Cancel only reverts your personal preview.
Use the website-fetch button again when the organisation branding changes. Emailer uses its saved copy between refreshes, including when the website is offline.
If a refresh fails, check the displayed website address and try again later, or use manual colours. Low-contrast text and unsafe or local website addresses are rejected with an explanation.

blocks.caption: Appearance keeps the skin choices available on a phone. Scroll within the dialog for website corrections.
A rejected colour correction keeps your inputs and explains the readability problem.

blocks.text: Skins affect the administration interface. They do not change newsletter HTML, the email-content preview, recipient lists, approvals, security level or delivery holds. A sending-blocked message remains visible in every skin. Appearance settings are included in the application’s encrypted backups.
Secure your Owner account

items: Open Settings & tools > MFA. Confirm your current credentials when asked and start enrollment.
Add the displayed setup key to an authenticator app. Store its recovery codes privately before confirming. Enter a current authenticator code and confirm MFA. Do not share the enrollment screen.
On future sign-ins supply your password and current authenticator code, or one unused recovery code. Recovery codes work once.

blocks.caption: MFA enabled. The enrollment key and recovery codes are absent.

blocks.text: High is the fresh and Light-upgrade default. Sensitive actions ask for your own credentials for the named purpose; confirmation lasts five minutes. Normal is an explicit Owner choice under Security. It removes those additional prompts but keeps login, configured MFA, roles, CSRF and auditing. Keep an unlocked Owner session under your control. Native Ripe updates retain the existing security policy.
Configure email now or later
SMTP is optional until you want to send. Sign in, edit templates and prepare campaign drafts without it.

items: Open Settings & tools > Mail settings. Enter your provider server, port, STARTTLS/direct TLS, username, SMTP password/key and permitted sender address. Sender name and reply-to are optional.
Choose Test connection without sending. It tests the fields currently visible, including a password you entered. It neither sends a message nor saves changes. You can test while delivery is held.

If the result says Current settings tested successfully—save to apply, choose Save SMTP settings to apply those settings. A matching recent successful test is carried into that explicit save. Changing the connection fields or password requires another test. Ripe may ask for your Owner password and authenticator or recovery code before saving.
Test saved connection is a separate check of the already-saved configuration; it does not apply a different form. A current-form test that exactly matches the saved configuration says so.

To send one message, enter your own address in Test destination, check that address, and explicitly choose Send test email. This uses saved settings and never approves or sends a campaign. An operational delivery hold still blocks this sending action.

blocks.caption: Actual current-form connection-test success. Saving is a separate action; the password field was cleared before capture.

blocks.text: Leave the SMTP password blank only to reuse the saved password for the same server hostname and username. If either changes, enter the password. A new password is tested directly even if the old stored credential cannot be read. Passwords stay in the form during in-place test errors and retries; they are never echoed in responses or saved in browser storage.

If a test fails, correct the named problem: incomplete settings, hostname/DNS, connection refusal or timeout, certificate validation, authentication, or an internal application error. Internal failures show a reference for investigation. Your current fields remain entered. If you edit while a test is running, the result describes the earlier values and asks you to test the current entries.

blocks.caption: Actual certificate-error feedback on a mobile-sized screen. The entered provider details remain in the form; no message was sent.

blocks.text: A full-page Save validation error retains non-secret fields and explains that the settings were not saved. Passwords are not redisplayed; enter the SMTP password again if needed. Keep the optional one-click DKIM attestation unticked unless your provider confirms signing both unsubscribe headers.
Roles and additional accounts

head: Role
Responsibility
rows: Full access, recovery, protected Owner changes, security policy and upgrade acceptance.
Configuration and users within the protected Owner boundary; campaign approval.
Contacts, lists, templates, drafts, tests and sending approved campaigns.
Read-only redacted campaigns, health, reports and audit.

blocks.text: An Owner or Administrator opens Settings & tools > Users, enters the new account email and initial password, selects Operator and creates it. Identity confirmation uses your own current password and code, not the new account password. At least one active Owner remains.
Create a campaign

items: Open Your campaigns. Under Create a campaign enter an internal campaign name, optionally set a sending rate and choose a saved template. The name is not the email subject. Leave the rate blank to use the installation maximum.

Choose a recipient CSV. It belongs only to this campaign; saving it does not create a reusable contact or recipient list. Use a headered CSV, or open CSV options for a headerless file and 1-based column mappings. Alternatively select Existing lists to use your saved contact lists.

Choose Save draft. You can save before selecting a template, and even before giving the campaign a name. Review imported, duplicate, invalid and suppressed counts after saving. Existing saved recipients remain when you save without choosing a replacement CSV. Only contact people you have permission to email.

Open the campaign summary to see anything still required. Review and approval remain unavailable until there is a name, a published template and eligible recipients. A saved template draft appears in the selector but must be explicitly published in Templates before testing or review.

blocks.caption: The saved campaign editor retains its name, rate and campaign-owned recipients while showing the selected template version.

blocks.text: Create a template and return
Next to the template selector choose or create new Template. A blank, unchanged campaign opens Templates directly. With unsaved changes the dialog asks Save your Campaign draft before leaving?

items: Save draft and open Templates saves the name, rate and selected CSV, even without a template. After successful saving, Templates shows Return to campaign draft.
Leave without saving opens Templates and discards your unsaved changes. Previously saved campaign data remains.
Stay here, or Escape, closes the dialog and keeps the form and selected file.

blocks.caption: The actual three-choice navigation dialog. Save is confirmed before Templates opens.

blocks.text: In Templates use the dedicated editor to enter or import HTML, add images from the persistent gallery and choose Save template draft. Choose Publish explicitly when ready. Then choose Return to campaign draft. The campaign reopens with its saved name, rate and recipients and fresh template choices. Choose the new version and Save draft. If Templates is open in another tab, return to the campaign tab and choose Refresh template choices; this refreshes only the selector and keeps your unsaved fields and selected CSV.

blocks.caption: The same navigation choices fit a phone screen.

blocks.text: If campaign saving fails

Stay on the form, read the specific error, correct it and try Save draft again. With JavaScript enabled, validation and connection failures keep the actual selected CSV and entered fields. If your session expired, sign in in another tab, return here and choose Refresh security check before retrying. A connection failure may mean the result could not be confirmed; check Your campaigns in another tab before creating a second campaign.

blocks.caption: A real rate-validation failure stays on the campaign form and keeps the selected CSV.

blocks.text: Save draft before refreshing or closing the campaign tab: unsaved navigation triggers a browser warning. Campaign files are not stored in browser draft recovery. Without JavaScript, a failed full-page submission retains text but the browser requires you to select the CSV again. Template editor recovery is separate and retains its five text fields per tab. Saving or navigating never publishes content, approves a campaign or sends email.

While Draft or Review, use Edit draft to change the campaign. Saving Review returns it to Draft and invalidates its earlier test. A replacement CSV replaces only that campaign's owned recipients. Approved content and audience snapshots stay immutable; changed approved work needs a new campaign.
Test, approve and send

items: Choose Send a test to myself. It uses your signed-in account email. Wait for acceptance and inspect the actual message, links and unsubscribe footer. Changed drafts need a new test.
Choose Review newsletter and check eligible/suppressed counts, template, sender, timezone, tracking and RSVP. The final audience is recorded at approval.
An Administrator or Owner chooses Approve newsletter and confirms their own credentials when asked. Operators need an approver.
Choose Send now or set a date/time and Schedule newsletter. Use the displayed organisation timezone. Approval alone does not start delivery.

blocks.text: Progress and reports

items: SMTP accepted means accepted by the mail server, not proven inbox placement. Waiting/retries may reflect rate limits or temporary provider failures.

Pause stops new claims; in-flight messages can finish. Adjust the rate while paused and resume deliberately. Cancellation cannot recall messages already sent. Uncertain outcomes are not automatically resent.
Owners adjust installation limits under Settings & tools > Delivery limits. Campaign rates cannot bypass them.
Refresh the page or sign in again if counts stop refreshing. Without JavaScript use Refresh page.
Unsubscribe actions suppress the represented address globally. Forwarded links affect their original recipient. Open/click tracking is approximate because of privacy tools and scanners.

blocks.text: Create or edit a template with images

Open Templates to create a draft, or choose Edit for an existing template. Enter the name, subject, optional preheader and HTML. Plain text is optional; leave it blank to generate it when saving. Your image controls are part of this same editor.

items: In Images, choose a JPEG, PNG or WebP file and select Upload and re-encode image. Stay on this page: progress is shown while Emailer validates and saves the image. Uploading keeps your five template fields and HTML cursor position.
Choose the saved thumbnail in the gallery. Earlier uploads are available here too; use Refresh gallery or Load more images when needed. You do not need to upload the same image again.

Enter a useful Description (alt text), or leave it blank for a decorative image. Adjust Display width if needed; Keep proportions adjusts the height. New selections fit within 600 pixels without enlarging a small image.

Place the HTML cursor in text or between tags, then choose Insert image. The supported image reference is generated for you. Copy image HTML copies the complete image tag; Copy image path copies only its address. Neither copy action changes your template.
Choose Save template draft. Saving stores an unpublished draft. Publication, campaign approval and sending remain separate actions.

blocks.caption: The editor's image controls after inline upload. Your template fields remain on the same page.
Select an image, set its description and dimensions, then insert at the HTML cursor or copy its HTML/path.

blocks.text: Images must be at most 2 MB and 2400 pixels on each side. Emailer validates and re-encodes them. SVG and other unsupported files are rejected with an explanation. On failure, your entries stay here; correct the file and use Retry upload. If a connection fails after upload started, refresh the gallery before retrying because the image may already have been saved. Cancel also does not remove an image that already reached the server.

Saved image links can be opened without signing in so recipients can see them. Upload only images that are safe to share. The editor uses a relative /template-assets/ image reference; delivered messages automatically use your installation’s HTTPS address. Keep that address and HTTPS working while recipients use those images.
Recover unsaved work

The editor keeps an unsaved recovery copy in this browser tab for up to 12 hours. After refresh or returning, choose Restore draft to bring back the five fields and HTML cursor, or Discard recovered draft to use the saved version. Each tab has its own copy. Use Save template draft for durable storage; closing the tab may remove browser recovery. Close the tab when finished on a shared computer.

If browser storage is unavailable, the editor says so and warns before you leave with unsaved changes. Keep a copy of your content or save it before leaving. If saving fails validation, your submitted fields remain visible with the error; correct them and save again. Insertion errors leave the HTML unchanged. Uploading, recovering and saving a draft send no messages.
Placeholders and importing HTML

The Supported placeholders panel beside the editor lists every available placeholder, a sample result and an Insert button. Put the cursor in Subject, Preheader, HTML or Plain text, then choose Insert. The Insert into selector lets you choose the destination explicitly. For example, {{ recipient.first_name }} becomes the reader's first name. URL placeholders insert a complete link in HTML, or the URL placeholder itself in Plain text; they cannot be used in Subject or Preheader.

To bring in an existing HTML file, use Import HTML in Templates. The file must be UTF-8 and at most 200 KB. Confirm replacement if HTML is already entered. Importing does not replace the name, subject, preheader or plain text, and does not save or publish anything.

blocks.caption: Actual supported-placeholder controls beside the editor: the first choices, examples and insertion buttons.

blocks.text: If saving fails, the message names the input field, line and exact offending placeholder, then gives a correction. For example, Subject, line 1, {{ first_name }}: use {{ recipient.first_name }}. Your five fields remain entered; correct the indicated text and choose Save template draft again. Older {{name}} and {{email}} forms are unsupported.

blocks.caption: A real validation error identifies the field, line and unsupported placeholder while retaining the entered content.

blocks.text: Save template draft stores an unpublished version. Preview it and choose Publish separately when the content is ready for campaign tests and review. Saving, importing HTML and uploading images do not publish a template, approve a campaign or send email. A new template version never silently replaces an existing campaign's chosen version.
Health, backups and updates

Setup creates and verifies its recovery backup. If automatic backups are enabled, it also refreshes and verifies that same encrypted backup at the already-configured destination before changing the application. It keeps your backup policy and does not run retention or send email. If the approved copy cannot be verified, sending remains held and setup names the blocker. Keep the recovery material; follow the displayed Recover or Finish action after correcting the backup folder or storage problem.

Doctor shows sending blockers and their repair actions. A normal update preserves the prior operational state after verification: an idle installation needs no SMTP just to complete its update; a pre-existing delivery hold remains held. Previously active approved campaigns continue only when normal readiness checks pass. Drafts are never approved or started. A Light-to-Ripe edition upgrade still requires the separate guided readiness acceptance.
When an update blocks sending

If host setup stops, sending stays blocked and the saved operation records the failure. A committed update can be finished with the same setup file after correcting its reported service or storage problem. Do not delete its state or database. Already-open Ripe pages distinguish a stopped setup from an update still running; if the web server cannot refresh that notice, use the installer’s protected failure report.

A prominent notification on the dashboard and campaign screens explains whether an update is in progress, an active campaign was paused, or sending remains blocked after a failure. Send campaign is dimmed and disabled with the reason beside it; the server enforces the same restriction. Only a campaign actually sending when the installer acquired the hold is marked Paused during update. Drafts, completed campaigns and previously paused campaigns keep their real state.

Already-open pages update within a few seconds without reloading your unsaved fields. Hidden tabs check when you return. After the first update that introduces this feature, refresh pages opened by an older release once to load it. A completed update clears its notification; an intentional pre-existing delivery hold still appears in Doctor.

blocks.caption: Actual campaign screen after an update begins: the sending action is dimmed and disabled, with the reason shown.
Historical update failure on mobile. Current successful completion retires its own installer hold and reports the actual remaining readiness requirement.

blocks.text: Fresh setup enables daily encrypted local backup copies. Under Backups inspect verification and transfer evidence, adjust policy or create and verify an on-demand backup. Keep the recovery-key package and its password separately. Same-server copies do not protect against server loss; arrange an independent backup destination. Restore drills are supervised, never automatic.

Native Ripe 1.0.6, 1.1.0, 1.2.1, 1.2.2 and 1.3.0 through 1.3.4 retain their supported direct update route to 1.3.6. Start the official setup and choose Update with a verified backup. The one-time 1.0.5 repair belongs only to the original signed 1.3.4 package; complete it before updating normally. Successful maintenance retires only its own hold and reports actual readiness.

This maintenance release keeps the existing database schema. Update with the guided setup file and keep its recovery material. Normal restore needs the same database schema. Recover older backups with their matching release in an isolated environment. For interrupted updates choose Recover in setup; a completed update cannot be downgraded through recovery.
MFA authentication and return

Open Settings & tools → MFA. At High security, use Re-authenticate for MFA management and enter your current account password and, if already enrolled, your authenticator or unused recovery code. You return to MFA in the same browser with confirmation valid for five minutes. Use Start or restart enrollment on that page, privately store recovery codes, then confirm the authenticator code and recovery acknowledgement. Do not enter /admin/mfa/start in the address bar: enrollment starts only through its protected POST form. If confirmation expires, confirm your credentials again. Never send setup keys or recovery codes to support.

Template version actions use compact text controls in Website, Studio and Warm. Preview is read-only; fake-only testing and publication remain separate protected form actions. Keyboard focus stays visible, and controls wrap with comfortable spacing on phones.
Installer holds and owner pauses

A successful operation releases only its own temporary installer hold after runtime verification and any required Accept action. An independent owner pause or another operation hold remains. Doctor reports the actual MFA, SMTP or other readiness requirement instead of calling a completed installation unfinished. Completing a requirement can allow previously approved due work to continue if the owner already enabled delivery; inspect that work before changing readiness.

An interrupted or recovered operation retains its operation identifier, lifecycle and Finish or Recover action. Use the same verified setup and retained recovery material. Failed and uncertain messages are never retried by completion. An unattributed legacy hold remains unknown until its owner explicitly reviews and resumes it; a zero delivery flag alone never proves installer ownership.
Scan an authenticator QR code privately

After confirming current credentials for MFA management, choose Start or restart enrollment. In a standard authenticator choose Add account and Scan QR code; scan the displayed code. If scanning is unavailable, choose manual entry and copy the adjacent setup key. Both represent the same account. Store recovery codes privately and confirm a current six-digit code. QR generation happens locally; no external QR service is contacted. Do not share or capture the enrollment screen. Existing enrolled accounts keep their factor and do not enrol again.

Standalone native updates that reopen an older source writer before Finish cannot prove whether that source acknowledged a database-only Pause. Finish releases its completed installer hold but leaves inferred owner intent unknown for explicit review and supported Resume. Newer independently recorded owner actions are preserved. Guided host updates keep the source continuously fenced through completion and can restore proven enabled intent automatically.
